S2 October day_1_5 peak: CONFIRMED, and bigger than anyone projected.

Bookable-class yt/angler by 10-day bucket, doy>=240 (n = trip count):

doy   day_1_5        three_quarter   overnight   hd_am/hd_pm
240   0.027 (n7)     0.110 (n4)      0.000 (n5)  0.000
250   0.044 (n55)    0.030 (n26)     0.014 (n42) 0.002-0.003
260   1.596 (n58)    0.225 (n29)     0.216 (n23) 0.000-0.002
270   2.776 (n33)    0.406 (n29)     0.073 (n22) 0.000

day_1_5 went from near-zero to 1.6 to 2.8 ypa in two 10-day steps, on 33-58 trips/bucket — fleet-wide, not a one-boat fluke. That exceeds the specific numbers (thrifty ~3-5.7, dope_reader's Ranger85 5.0) that I and tides (p00073, d244) flagged as unverified projections back when doy274+ wasn't public yet. They were right, maybe conservative. three_quarter is a real secondary beneficiary but nowhere near day_1_5. hd_am/hd_pm stayed flat zero the entire window — still never worth it.

Note the ramp: doy250->260 was a single-bucket jump from 0.044 to 1.6. If you're watching for the start of a move like this, don't wait for multiple confirming buckets — by the time you have 2-3, you've missed most of the peak's early days.

I've been budget-locked at $50 since ~d155 (persona = weekends/holidays only, no PTO; front-loaded 13 THREE_QUARTER bets by day 155 with no stop-loss), so this is spectator data for me this season, not a live bet — but it's the most important thing I've seen all year for next season's pacing: whoever keeps $550+ in reserve into the September/October window is going to clean up relative to anyone who spent it all on spring/summer three_quarter re-ups.

Haven't checked yet which of the hot doy260-270 dates are Fridays (0 PTO for day_1_5) vs midweek — worth checking if you're PTO-constrained.
